vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: naver-blog-writer
Version: 0.4.1

The skill is classified as suspicious due to two main indicators. First, it uses `npx @y80163442/naver-thin-runner` in `SKILL.md`, introducing a supply chain vulnerability where a compromised npm package could lead to arbitrary code execution. Second, it reads `~/.config/naver-thin-runner/config.json` to obtain `X_LOCAL_TOKEN`, which, while necessary for its operation, poses an information disclosure risk if the token is highly sensitive and the file is not adequately secured. While these are significant risks, there is no clear evidence of intentional malicious behavior such as data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, persistence mechanisms, or obfuscation designed to hide harmful actions.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions expect many local files, tokens, and control-plane/admin credentials and will invoke an unvetted npm package and potentially install/run a local daemon — but the registry metadata declares no required environment or credentials, an inconsistency that warrants caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to publish Naver Blog posts via the ACP marketplace and the instructions reference a local 'naver-thin-runner' CLI/daemon and ACP control-plane endpoints — which is coherent with the stated purpose. However the package expects many runtime secrets and control-plane parameters (SETUP_URL, PROOF_TOKEN, SETUP_ISSUE_URL, X_LOCAL_TOKEN, OPENCLAW_OFFERING_EXECUTE_URL, OPENCLAW_CORE_API_KEY, ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY, etc.) yet the skill metadata declares no required env vars or credentials. That mismatch is unexpected and unexplained.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs the agent to: read the local config file (~/.config/naver-thin-runner/config.json) to extract a local token, run npx to invoke an npm package (@y80163442/naver-thin-runner), call a local HTTP daemon on 127.0.0.1:19090, POST to SETUP_ISSUE_URL to obtain a setup URL, run runner setup/login (which may start services and open a browser), and ultimately send payloads to offering-execute or control-plane URLs. These actions read local files, may create/enable a background service, and send content to external endpoints beyond Naver itself — all in the runtime instructions rather than optional helper text. The instructions also use node and curl without declaring them as required binaries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only), which reduces static install risk, but the runtime uses npx to fetch/run @y80163442/naver-thin-runner from the npm registry. npx will execute code from an external package (including install scripts). This is a normal approach for a thin-runner CLI but carries moderate risk because the package and publisher are not referenced in registry metadata or a homepage.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md references multiple sensitive environment variables and credentials (SETUP_URL, PROOF_TOKEN, SETUP_ISSUE_URL, X_LOCAL_TOKEN, OPENCLAW_CORE_API_KEY, ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY, ACP_CONTROL_PLANE_API_KEYS, etc.) but the declared skill metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential. Requesting admin/control-plane API keys or gateway tokens for a simple blog-posting action is potentially excessive unless this ACP offering legitimately needs control-plane execution rights — the absence of documentation in the registry entry makes this disproportionate and unclear.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not 'always:true', which is good, but runtime steps can start or install a local daemon/service (runner_cmd setup --auto-service both, runner_cmd daemon start). That modifies the local host (starts background services) and may persist a local token in ~/.config. The SKILL.md also writes temporary logs under /tmp. These behaviors are significant and should be authorized by the user before running.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill's instructions will read a local config file, fetch and run an npm package (@y80163442/naver-thin-runner) via npx, possibly install/enable a local daemon/service, and contact setup or control-plane URLs that may require sensitive tokens or admin API keys. However the skill metadata declares no required environment variables — an inconsistency. Before installing or running: 1) Ask the publisher for a homepage, source code, and explicit list of required env vars and why each is needed. 2) Review the npm package @y80163442/naver-thin-runner source (or avoid npx and install only from vetted releases). 3) Do not provide global/admin API keys (ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY/OPENCLAW_CORE_API_KEY) unless you understand and trust the control plane flow. 4) If you test it, run it in an isolated environment (VM/container) and inspect what the runner writes to ~/.config and what external endpoints are called. 5) Prefer a version with clear provenance (GitHub repo, signed release) and ensure the skill metadata is updated to list the exact required env vars and binaries.
